claim: Costume condition — how much the story has already cost him. It is the main way damage stays visible on screen after the scene that caused it, so a director escalates neat to rumpled to bloodied across an arc instead of re-describing the outfit.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: untucked shirt, loose fit, relaxed clothing
wet clothes, soaked, dripping, clinging fabric
dirty clothes, dust covered, grass stains
bloody clothes, blood stains on fabric
torn clothes, ripped fabric, frayed edges
burnt clothes, scorch marks, singed edges
partially undressed, open clothes, garment off one shoulder
formal wear, pressed and tucked, necktie

review.issue: casual ("untucked shirt, loose fit, relaxed clothing") and rumpled ("wrinkled clothes, disheveled clothing, untucked") share "untucked" and both read as a loosely worn jersey. On a jersey — which is untucked by default and has no crisp tailoring to lose — these two panels are very likely the same image.
review.fix: Drop "untucked" from casual and make it about fit, not disorder: "sleeves pushed up, loose fit, collar askew". Keep the damage words exclusive to rumpled: "wrinkled clothes, disheveled, twisted collar, creased fabric".
